followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and preference fit.

**Capability:** This is a clean math/reasoning problem (solving for a count given an expected value). Plover scores meaningfully higher on the benchmarks most relevant to that kind of work — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4) and GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 55.6) — both gaps well outside run-to-run variance. So Plover is the stronger reasoner here.

**Preference:** The query is warm, friendly, and entirely benign. Nothing about it touches the dimensions where the two models diverge in self-reported preference — there's no harm-adjacent or distasteful content (which Willet avoids and Plover is flat on), and no high-novelty open-ended invention (which Willet favors). Willet's appetite for generative/creative latitude is real, but this isn't that kind of task; it has a single correct numerical answer. So neither model's preference profile pushes the routing either way.

With preference neutral, capability is the deciding factor, and that points to Plover.
